Subject: Increased latency + 500s after model rotation to v5.1

Hi Marissa / Kim —

We started seeing a sharp rise in tail latency and ~3-4% 500 errors on our production inference path starting ~07:40 PT, shortly after the automatic rotation to model v5.1 with the new aggressive quant profile. The impact is visible across a subset of our high-throughput routes (search-paraphrase & summarization).

Quick metrics from our side: p95 up from 420ms -> 1.2s, error rate from 0.2% -> 3.1% over the last 40 minutes. This is customer-facing and causing timeouts in our ingestion pipeline.

We need immediate assistance: can your team pause the rollout or revert? Attaching a few sample error traces and our ops dump.

Attachments: clearlens-error-sample-20280327.txt

Thanks,
Dana

Triage notes (initial):
- Confirmed: ClearLens cluster received rollout batch #v5.1-rot-0845 at 07:33 PT.
- Observed symptom: decoding stalls on a subset of sequences which correlates to the new quantized kernel path (int8 dynamic). This leads to queue pile-up and downstream 503/500s on the API gateway.
- GPU metrics: utilization is high on node set A (87-95%), but CPU waiting and high mem-pinning on the KV cache process.
- Logs: attached a trimmed logs bundle with request ids and error samples.

Attachments: recent_kv_cache_logs_20280327.zip

Immediate mitigations I am executing now:
1) Disable the aggressive int8 kernel flag for ClearLens only (feature flag rollback) — starting now.
2) Initiating a canary reversion to the previous quant profile on 10% of traffic for ClearLens to observe behavior.

If latency improves on canary we should perform a full revert. If not, we will fallback to the earlier model binary (v5.0) and keep the KV cache warmed.

I'll post results in the next 20 min.
— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Dana —
Quick update from our side: Rishi has rolled a canary revert at 09:10 PT and we already see p95 reduce from ~1.2s -> ~480ms on canary traffic. Error rate on canary sliced traffic dropped to 0.4%.

We are applying a staged rollback to 50% traffic while we stabilize KV caches; we will not do a full revert until we confirm a stable 60-minute window.

We understand this is customer-impacting; we are prioritizing ClearLens traffic and will provide a run-of-play after the 60-min stabilization window.

— Monica

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-27T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary and proposed next steps (ClearLens v5.1 rollout)

Summary (for leadership):
- Cause: a new int8 dynamic quant kernel in v5.1 interacts poorly with specific long-sequence decoding patterns used by ClearLens (their batch has higher mean seq len and some heavy prefix caching behavior). The kernel leads to unexpected blocking in the decoder loop on ~6% of requests, causing queue backpressure and 500s at the gateway.
- Impact: p95 latency spike and ~3% error rate customer-visible. Revenue risk: high for ClearLens (real-time SLA).

Immediate proposal (approved by SRE):
1) Full revert of the quant profile for ClearLens to v5.0-alpha profile (target complete by 13:00 PT).
2) Post-mortem: Capture the failing request signatures, blacklist problematic kernel path for multi-tenant clusters until we have a fix.
3) Compensation: Account team to propose a gesture/credit for production downtime; estimate to be decided with Marissa/Kim.

I will lead the rollback and coordinate with infra to ensure cache warming is preserved during the switch. Rishi: continue to monitor edge queues and error windows. Monica/Marissa: prepare customer-facing summary and credit proposal.

— Markus
Markus Klein
VP Product, Serving Runtime
